name: Muttekopf
kurzbeschreibung: The Muttekopf (2,774 m) above Imst: Alpine Coaster, Imster Bergbahnen cable cars, cosy Muttekopfhütte at 1,934 m, and thrilling via ferratas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic Muttekopf is a 2,774-metre-high summit in the Lechtal Alps and the proud local mountain of the district capital Imst in the Tyrolean Oberland. Nestled within the expansive Muttekopf massif, the mountain region forms one of Tyrol's most versatile outdoor adventure and hiking terrains. From the valley station in Hoch-Imst, the Imster Bergbahnen chairlifts access the alpine terrain in two sections up to the Alpjoch at 2,050 metres above sea level. Featuring the world's longest alpine roller coaster – the Alpine Coaster Imst –, the historic Muttekopfhütte, and daring via ferratas, the mountain delights families and seasoned alpinists alike.

Alpine Coaster, Hiking & Mountain Huts

The primary family highlight is the world-renowned Alpine Coaster Imst: stretching 3,525 metres in track length, it ranks as the longest tracked alpine coaster in the Alps. Starting from the middle station at the Untermarkter Alm (1,500 m), riders zoom over 500 vertical metres through sweeping curves, waves, and 360-degree loops down to Hoch-Imst. Above the cable car, a high-alpine arena opens up: positioned on a sunny rock shelf at 1,934 metres is the historic Muttekopfhütte of the Austrian Alpine Club (ÖAV). From the hut, the marked normal route ascends through the Scharnitzkar cirque in about 2.5 hours to the Muttekopf summit (2,774 m), rewarding hikers with panoramic vistas across the Ötztal, Stubai, and Lechtal Alps and the Zugspitze. Climbers tackle the challenging Waterfall Via Ferrata in the Rosengartenschlucht and the alpine Muttekopf-Klettersteig (Grade C).

Visit & Arrival

The Imster Bergbahnen lifts and the Alpine Coaster operate during the summer season from early May to late October daily from 09:00 to 17:00 (winter offers skiing and tobogganing). Summer rates (2025/2026): Single Alpine Coaster ride including lift ascent: Adults €17.50, children (born 2010–2018) €13.00; Cable car return to Alpjoch: Adults €24.00, children €14.50. Discounts available with the Urlaubsticket Imst. Arrival by car: Via the A12 autobahn, exit Imst, and follow signs to Hoch-Imst (Teilwiesen 8); spacious free car parks are located at the valley station. By public transport: Rail (ÖBB) to Imst-Pitztal station, then local Imst town bus directly to Hoch-Imst valley station.

Tips

The cable car to the Untermarkter Alm is fully accessible; the alpine hut at the middle station boasts a sunny terrace with a playground. Hikers can begin their excursion through the Rosengartenschlucht gorge, which starts right in the town centre of Imst with roaring waters and romantic wooden walkways.
